summary: This follow-up correctly fixes both blocking findings from PR #54's prior audit. The cross-user leak is closed by threading an explicit scope (the Supabase auth user id) through every offline-queue function and keying a separate IndexedDB store per scope with no unscoped fallback, and WorkProgressClient gates every queue read/write on scope being resolved rather than defaulting to a shared store. The sync race is closed with a real mutex keyed by scope in a module-level Map: because the outer function is synchronous and JS async functions run synchronously up to their first await, the lock is guaranteed to be visible to a second concurrent call before that call can start its own drain, verified by a concurrent-sync test that asserts exactly one POST. The bonus max-attempt cap correctly marks permanently-failing entries 'failed' and excludes them from the automatic retry loop. New tests (cross-user isolation, concurrent dedupe, max-attempts) are real and exercise the actual module against a real IndexedDB, not mocks of the module's own logic. The diff is additive/isolated (no schema, migrations, auth/permission/payment/rls paths, or .github/workflows changes), consistent with its pre-classified tier1 status.
issues: The sync mutex (syncLocks Map) is per JS module instance, i.e. per browser tab -- it does not prevent two tabs of the same signed-in user open simultaneously from both draining the queue and double-POSTing the same entry. This is a narrower but related race than the one the audit flagged (same-tab remount/multiple 'online' events), not addressed here.

Entries that hit MAX_SYNC_ATTEMPTS and are marked 'failed' have no UI affordance to delete or manually retry them (removeQueuedWorkProgressEntry exists but isn't wired into WorkProgressClient) -- they persist in the queued-entries list indefinitely as dead weight. Minor UX gap, not a correctness or security issue.
